title: When Facts Change, Which Decisions Break? Dependency-Aware Context Graphs for Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.19859v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When an observed fact changes, an agent must identify and repair the decisions that depend on it while preserving unaffected outputs. We investigate the reliability-cost trade-off of field-level dependency graphs extracted from actual agent read traces. A controlled benchmark spans three executable workflow domains and four successive updates, with independent imperative and expression-based references. Across 120 workflows, two models and two repeated runs, we compare full recomputation, rolling summary memory, lexical retrieval, trace-extracted dependencies and verified dependency upper bounds. Trace-derived graphs reduce reviewed decisions and estimated total cost, but omitted alternative supports and missing repair context can reduce complete-plan correctness. Paired ablations isolate the effects of edge deletion, spurious edges, transitive propagation and context scope. An exploratory enhancement supplies the existing record ID/fiel

translated_title: 当事实发生变化时，哪些决策会失效？面向智能体的依赖感知上下文图
translated_abstract: 当观测到的事实发生变化时，智能体必须识别并修复依赖于该事实的决策，同时保持未受影响的输出不变。我们研究了从智能体实际读取轨迹中提取的字段级依赖图的可靠性-成本权衡。受控基准涵盖三个可执行的工作流领域和四次连续更新，并配有独立的命令式和基于表达式的参考实现。在涵盖120个工作流、两个模型和两次重复运行的实验中，我们比较了完全重计算、滚动摘要记忆、词汇检索、轨迹提取依赖以及经过验证的依赖上界等方法。结果表明，由轨迹推导的依赖图减少了需要审查的决策数量和估计总成本，但遗漏的替代支持路径和缺失的修复上下文可能会降低完整计划的正确性。成对消融实验分离了边删除、虚假边、传递性传播和上下文范围的影响。一项探索性增强方法提供了现有的记录ID/字段……
tldr: 该论文提出从智能体的实际读取轨迹中提取字段级依赖图，用于在事实变化时识别需要修复的决策，在降低审查决策数量和总成本的同时，也揭示了依赖图遗漏替代支持和修复上下文可能损害完整计划正确性的可靠性-成本权衡。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes extracting field-level dependency graphs from actual agent read traces to identify which decisions break when facts change, showing that such graphs reduce the number of reviewed decisions and estimated total cost, while revealing a reliability-cost trade-off where omitted alternative supports and missing repair context can compromise complete-plan correctness.
